key_insight: Reported gains from randomly perturbing pretrained language models may not require discovering hidden task-specific experts in weight space. Keeping the model frozen and adding a random bias to its output logits can match or exceed full-weight perturbations.
problem_solved: Tests whether the gains attributed to the Neural Thickets hypothesis actually require its proposed weight-space explanation, or can arise from simpler changes to model outputs.
method: Reproduce the reported improvements from random Gaussian weight perturbations.
Restrict perturbations to a single decoder block and measure how much improvement remains.
Compare against a fully frozen model with a random bias added to its output logits.
impact: The findings challenge a geometric explanation for the reported gains and highlight a simpler baseline practitioners should test before modifying model weights. Output-level interventions may deliver comparable improvements without weight perturbations.
visual_elements: Three-path diagram comparing full-weight perturbation, single-block perturbation, and frozen-model logit bias.
Transformer schematic highlighting all decoder blocks, one decoder block, or only the output logits.
Qualitative comparison chart showing that single-block perturbation recovers much of the gain and logit bias can match or exceed full-weight perturbation.
Hypothesis-versus-evidence panel contrasting hidden weight-space experts with the frozen-model result.
paper_title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
paper_authors: Nicolas Dufour, Elouan Gardès, Amil Dravid, Patrick Pérez, Loic Landrieu
